newsitem.title: UK: UK carpet and sofa shops to gain from windfalls.
newsitem.headline: UK carpet and sofa shops to gain from windfalls.

text.p: Millions of British consumers getting big cash windfalls from building society flotations this year are likely to spend their money on a new carpet or furniture, according to a new study.
Consumers are set to receive the cash by selling free shares they receive from mutually-owned mortgage lenders, which are converting to listed companies.
The largest, Halifax Plc, this week paid out an average 2,294 stg worth of shares to its members when it made its debut on the London Stock Exchange on Monday.

"These lump sums should prove a support to the housing market but the average size of cash receipts of between 1,500 and 2,000 stg also equates neatly to the cost of a new three piece suite or a carpet," retail consultants Verdict said on Wednesday.
As a result the furniture and carpet markets, worth almost nine billion stg in 1996, will grow faster than all retail sales in both 1997 and 1998, Verdict predicted.
But the upturn will not be a repeat of the credit-fuelled 1980's boom. "Consumers in the 1990s are much more cautious and will not over-extend themselves again," Verdict said.
But the cash windfalls, plus the housing upturn will benefit fitted carpets and kitchens, which will see growth again after a long period of decline.
The market for upholstered furniture has traditionally been fragmented, but DFS Furnituure Plc has established market leadership and its competitors are lagging some way behind, the report said.

Verdict sees ample scope for mergers and acquisitions in this sector of the market. "Consolidation among upholstered furniture manufacturers is likely to follow, creating larger companies who are better able to deal with the big multiple retailers."
Verdict also predicts that interest-free credit will steadily diminish in importance in the furniture market.
In carpets, Carpetright Plc and Allied Carpets Group Plc already dominate, and together have around a quarter of the market.
Verdict estimates that Carpetright increased its market share by 23 percent last year and is now challenging Allied for market leadership. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
